Subject: Post-demo: encryption and key management options for AcmeCloud

Hi Oliver — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so everything is in one thread.

Recap from our call:
- Use case: tenant classification and policy routing for PII-sensitive requests; logging for debug + audit.
- Requirements you called out: at-rest encryption with customer control over keys, KMS integration (preferred), in-transit TLS >=1.2, and 13-month retention for full request logs, shorter retention for debug artifacts.
- Constraints: offline HSM for very sensitive workflows is desirable for some teams; SOC2 audit coming up in Q3.

Attachments: a short one-pager on KMS/HSM options and a matrix comparing key-management workflows (attached).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (60m) with your security engineers to walk KMS flow and HSM support — can we book for next week?
2) Share our SOC2 encryption evidence and the logs-retention options (attached).
3) If KMS is required, decide whether to use:
   - Redwood-managed envelope keys (we manage CMKs, customer controls access via policies), or
   - Customer-managed keys (integrate with your KMS via IAM / external key encryption), or
   - Dedicated HSM (on-prem or cloud HSM) for FIPS-level separation.

Would you be able to confirm who on your side should be in the deep-dive? I penciled in a tentative window (see calendar invite if it helps).

Thanks — Ben

Ben — thanks for the write-up and the attachments, that helps. A few clarifying points from our security team: 

1) For customer-managed keys we need to understand whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext model input/outputs when you use our CMKs. Our security folks flagged a concern about key wrapping vs. direct encryption at the storage layer.
2) For HSM: we don't need on-prem HSM for the initial rollout. Cloud HSM is preferred but must provide customer-controlled key import and rotation.
3) Logs: retention policy needs to support a deletion lifecycle that can be triggered by us; in particular we need a way to purge PII-derived logs earlier than the default retention in case of a legal hold expiration.

Can Aditya and Marissa join the deep-dive? Also can you send the high-level sequence diagram for a request encrypted with our KMS (covering transit, at-rest, and cache eviction)?

Hi Oliver — Aditya on Redwood's Security & Integrations team here. Thanks for the questions; below are terse answers and I'll expand in the deep-dive with diagrams.

Short answers:
- Does Redwood see plaintext when customer-managed KMS is used? No, if you choose customer-managed envelope encryption our service will only see encrypted keys (we perform envelope encryption where the data key is encrypted with your CMK and Redwood stores only the wrapped key). Plaintext data keys are kept in memory on the serving node and are never persisted to disk; disk at-rest content is encrypted with the data key.
- Key wrapping vs direct encryption: we support both envelope (recommended) and direct per-object encryption depending on performance needs. Envelope gives you full control of the root CMK and audit trail on your KMS; we never transmit your CMK off your KMS.
- HSM / Cloud HSM options: we support integrations with major cloud KMS providers that back their keys with HSM (Google Cloud KMS, AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys, Azure Key Vault HSM). For strict separation we offer a dedicated HSM option as part of Redwood Private / Dedicated where keys are imported into a customer-controlled HSM and Redwood is granted only ephemeral usage permissions.
- Logs & retention: we can expose an API for log deletion calls and support TTL policies per-tenant. For legal hold scenarios we can also snapshot logs into an immutable archive and retain per agreement.

I attached a short checklist for the deep-dive; Ben will follow up with a calendar invite containing a preliminary agenda.

Cheers — Aditya
